root_cause_label: False Theorem from Single Airline (Confuses A100's 99-Day Gap with No-Flight Gap Overall)
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent makes a false logical leap at step 7 — equating the 99-day intra-period gap of the 100-day airline with a global 99-day no-flight guarantee — and then hardcodes 99 into the script without verifying against adversarial offset configurations, producing the wrong answer (correct is 79).
t_err_evidence: In step 7 the agent concludes: 'Yes, because even if one company has a flight every 100 days, there are 99 days between consecutive flights from that company alone. So regardless of the other companies, there are always at least 99 consecutive days without flights from company 1.' This conflates a single-airline intra-period gap with a global multi-airline no-flight gap — the key unverified wrong assumption.
t_commit_evidence: In step 8 the agent creates /app/airline_analysis.py with hardcoded return value of 100 - 1 = 99 and writes that result to results.txt. From this point the wrong answer is encoded in the output file and the agent will not revisit the logic.
trigger_explanation: The agent correctly identifies in step 6 that offsets must be explored adversarially, but at step 7 it abandons that plan and instead asserts — without verification — that company 1's 99-day intra-period gap constitutes a global flight-free guarantee. This is a false premise: the 120-day and 150-day airlines can schedule departures within those 99 days, compressing the guaranteed global no-flight run. The correct answer (79) requires exhaustive offset analysis which the agent explicitly planned but never executed.
forewarning_evidence: Step 5 produces a wraparound gap of -1 (an unexpected/nonsensical negative gap), signaling a boundary/offset confusion. Step 6 contains extensive self-doubt language explicitly noting the zero-offset assumption is wrong and that offsets must be enumerated — 'But I need to reconsider the problem... this is not necessarily the case' — yet the agent drops this plan at step 7.
